item.text: {"representations":[{"case_ref":"sample_b977d7c729a9dca4","text":"Across March 30–April 12, active minutes fell abruptly from the 28-day baseline mean of 54.4 to 9.4/day (−45; −83%), remaining 8–12 every day without recovery, on weekdays and weekends alike. Activity still began at 21:00. Low movement rose from 449.6 to 602 minutes/day (+152; +34%): ten daily bouts lengthened from roughly 44–47 to 59–61 minutes, separated by five-minute gaps, extending from 10:00 to about 20:40–20:53 instead of about 18:00–18:27. A slight downward trend did not restore baseline levels. Despite these changes, steps stayed near baseline (8,029 versus 8,015/day), as did sleep (470.6 versus 469.8 minutes), resting heart rate (55.9 versus 55.8 bpm), and RMSSD (44.9 versus 45.1 ms). Sleep starts remained around 22:42–22:57, with 07:00 waking and little weekday/weekend separation. Starts shifted from baseline 22:32–22:46 to 00:32–00:43, while waking stayed at 07:00. On April 6–12, starts returned to 22:35–22:46 and sleep to 474–485 minutes (mean 480), sustaining recovery through the final day. The overall mean of 421.6 minutes (−59.2) and rising trend therefore reflect a step back to baseline, rather than gradual recovery.
